title: How Price replaced Willie the Lion Smith for Europe in 1948
summary: His first trip to Europe came by accident when Mayers switched Willie the Lion's ticket to him, causing confusion for Panassie.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Was that your first time in Europe?
Yep. 1948. It was very, very interesting. We were supposed to land in...at....what the hell were we

supposed to do, we were supposed to land in Nice. But then they couldn't land in Nice because of the conditions and we had to go all the way back to Orly Airport in Paris and we landed in Paris. Panassié was having a fit. Well actually, do you know that I went to Europe that year by accident. Again, you see. So perhaps fate has played a role with me on many evenings in my life and many points in my life, just as the lady saying to me, "Do you want to do some work?" Willie "the Lion" Smith was slated to go to Europe and Willie didn't go. And Mayers asked me to come. He didn't let Panassié know because days of communication were, you know what I mean, you write a letter today and you get an answer next...whatever you got the answer it would be too late to do whatever you wanted to do. So they just simply switched Willie "the Lion's" ticket over to me and I went in his stead. And it really created a furor...and Johnny (Zimmer?) later told me, and then I think they wrote about how confusing it was, that they were looking for Willie "the Lion" Smith and when they called on the telephone they were trying to determine who the replacement for Willie "the Lion" Smith was and Panssié was, you know, yelling and the producer was yelling, and they said, "Pappy Drake----Pappy Rice".....they didn't know what name it was. that they (Laughter.) So finally it dawned on Hugues, were saying
"Sammy Price." He says, "Merveilleux Mayers" , you know, 'he's so marvelous with his ideas.' So, and that's how I happened to get to Europe..that first time.
